newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower ahead of cabinet reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower ahead of cabinet reshuffle.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended slightly lower on Tuesday as a bitter political row over the government's ability to fight crime -- and the extent of an expected cabinet reshuffle -- fuelled financial market jitters, brokers said.

Sentiment stabilised somewhat after parliament rejected a non-binding, opposition motion that would have urged President Lee Teng-hui to sack Premier Lien Chan over his cabinet's failure to solve a spate of horrific crimes, brokers added.
The weighted index see-sawed through the morning and closed 14.52 points or 0.18 percent lower at 7,952.12, failing to recover from Monday's huge politically inspired downturn.

Plagued by uncertainty amid a volatile public row over crime ahead of the ruling Nationalist Party's cabinet reshuffle, the index tumbled 3.72 percent on Monday as presumed support at 8,000 points evaporated. Tuesday saw some profit-taking.
"Some investors took the opportunity of Monday's big fall to buy cheaper shares, and parliament's rejection restored some confidence," said National Securities fund manager Allen Huang.

The parliamentary motion's defeat -- the second in a week -- meant Lien likely would propose only a modest reshuffle of his cabinet at a meeting on Wednesday of the Nationalist Party's central standing committee.

Lien late on Monday appeared ready to heed growing demands for his head, telling a television call-in show that he was willing to step down -- but not before crucial constitutional reforms are enacted by the National Assembly in July.
Paper shares plunged by 2.38 percent on Tuesday, with Taiwan Pulp and Paper losing T$1.80 to T$25.10.
But the heavily weighted financials attracted mild institutional bargain-hunting, gaining 0.31 percent.
"It is natural for various groups or individuals to try to boost the market after such a big fall on Monday," said David Yu, vice president of International Investment Trust.
